high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I love eating and often find myself eating more than feels like enough. A good meal can draw me into another portion even after I am comfortably satisfied. Enjoyment of eating is part of my experience as well as the tendency to go beyond the amount I wanted.

Some things I do leave me unsure why I did them. Looking back at an ordinary action, I may be unable to explain my own reason for taking it. This puzzlement can occur without a dramatic event or a complicated decision.

I also do things I later regret. After the immediate appeal has passed, I can wish I had not made a purchase, sent a remark or chosen an activity. This concerns my reaction to my own action rather than disappointment at every unfavorable outcome.

Temptations can be hard to resist, and my cravings can lead me to overindulge or have a bout of taking far more of a pleasure than intended. I sometimes splurge on optional purchases and can spend more than my resources comfortably allow.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My work habits, honesty, kindness, anxiety and knowledge can vary independently. I can describe overindulgence coherently; it does not establish a diagnosis, body size, malicious intent, universal irresponsibility or actual failure to follow an experimental instruction.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary activities and resources. I rarely eat more than feels like enough, and I do not have a special love of eating as an activity. Food can serve an ordinary practical place in my day without becoming a particular source of delight. I generally finish a meal without feeling that I took too much.

I usually understand why I do the everyday things I choose. Looking back at an action, I can generally identify what led me to it. My own behavior seldom leaves me puzzled about a reason that remains entirely unclear to me.

I rarely do things I later regret. After an ordinary purchase, remark or activity, I generally remain content with having acted as I did. An outcome can still disappoint me without making me wish I could undo my own choice.

I can usually resist temptations and control cravings, even with something appealing within reach. Overindulgence and binges are uncommon for me. I keep purchases within what I can afford and very rarely splurge on optional luxuries, including when a lavish purchase would be possible.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My work habits, honesty, kindness, anxiety and knowledge can vary independently. Restraint does not require joylessness, wealth, a restrictive diet, perfect planning, a diagnosis or being successful in every other part of life.
